reviewed_paths.title: Conventional — language-model training, checkpoints and export
reviewed_paths.boundary: Entire train module reviewed. Dataset assigns whole shards among workers, makes context+1 windows and pads the final remainder with ignored labels. Runtime provider, model architecture, optimizer/library internals, distributed counting accuracy and resumability acceptance remain separate. Nothing was trained or exported during this research.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — request routing before local authorization
reviewed_paths.boundary: Ordering is taken from Program.cs. Proxy requests finish before the local rate limiter, exception envelope and authentication middleware. This does not establish the upstream authorization configuration. Endpoint routing/framework internals, browser login provider and code-model interception remain separately inspectable boundaries.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — resolve request tenant and workspace
reviewed_paths.boundary: Tenant resolution is not authorization. ApiKeyTenantResolver is registered in all modes; non-header modes enforce identity in separate middleware. Workspace selection is checked against membership and mutates only the request principal, not the immutable login ticket. SQL membership function and browser ticket validation remain nested.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — route, browser membership and platform enforcement
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete middleware reviewed. SameOrigin compares supplied Origin scheme/authority against current request; without Origin it accepts Sec-Fetch-Site=same-origin or X-Laplace-Request=1. Public routes still reject a supplied invalid key. Webhook bypass here is not webhook-signature verification. Header mode permits unresolved header tenants; deployment mode is configuration, not inferred from source.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — platform permission and serialized role changes
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete platform store and policy reviewed. DevPrincipalActive makes HasCredential return true before token comparison, irrespective of supplied credentials; tenant resolution has a narrower no-credential dev fallback. Operator token comparison is fixed-time after equal-length check. Platform roles and workspace membership are separate tables/decisions; this is not semantic evidence standing.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — API-key issue, validation, touch and revocation
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete key service and both stores reviewed. Validation performs a read then separate usage write; revocation is not transactionally rechecked before returning the previously read record. In-memory touch/revoke use dictionary read/replace operations and do not provide an atomic compare-update across both. PostgreSQL issue uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING; tenant foreign-key violation has a specific error. Plaintext is returned by issuance, not stored by these stores.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — workspace ownership before checkout and subscription
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete ownership middleware reviewed. It validates request ownership and selected subscription prerequisites; it does not itself charge, grant entitlement or reserve a unique subscription transaction. Duplicate-property detection applies only to queried identity fields. Existing-subscription read and downstream purchase are separate operations. Billing enforcement bypass is a different option whose default is true in AppComposition.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — fixed-origin Refactor streaming proxy
reviewed_paths.boundary: Entire proxy reviewed. It adds no credential, but forwards incoming end-to-end Authorization/Cookie headers unless excluded by Connection. Upstream authentication is a separate boundary. It does not support CONNECT or protocol upgrade. Client-owned cancellation controls streams; pooled buffers are returned in finally.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — quote creation and checkout handoff
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete BillingOrchestrator preflight body reviewed. Quote persistence, provider call and final update are separate effects; exception/cancellation can leave the earlier pending quote. Stripe gateway internals, catalog price authority and provider acceptance remain separate. TryApproveQuoteAsync changes a found quote to approved; route authorization is outside that method.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — billing admission and credit debit
reviewed_paths.boundary: Gate checks and plan debit do not reserve a quote in the transaction that executes an operation. Debit can precede a failed quote write or later operation failure. Quote updates are unconditional upserts; concurrent admission of the same unconsumed approved quote is not excluded here. A billing gate is not a native resource grant, cognition completion or successful effect receipt.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — quote consumption before inference and separate ledger
reviewed_paths.boundary: Reviewed concrete endpoint ordering and both PostgreSQL stores. MarkConsumedAndRecordAsync does not compare-and-set consumed=false and does not share a transaction across quote and ledger updates. It records an ExecutedAt timestamp before later inference; the row alone is not proof that inference completed.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — plan-credit debit in each store
reviewed_paths.boundary: Both concrete debit bodies reviewed. PostgreSQL SQL does not check period_start <= now, unlike the in-memory branch. Both order by credit limit, not remaining headroom despite the SQL comment. SQL has no own positive-unit guard; the reviewed C# adapter supplies one. Debit is one database statement, separate from quote approval/consumption and operation execution. Installed SQL and concurrency acceptance were not tested.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — PostgreSQL resource ownership equation
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete resource-equation source reviewed. It returns configuration values; it does not reserve memory or enforce every executor allocation. Topology detection and settings application remain nested. Effective cache size is shared plus OS cache, not an extra allocation. The equation alone does not prove a hard memory ceiling.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — discover and verify task-shape structures
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete PostgreSQL task_shape.c orchestration/helpers reviewed. Type-8 trajectory structure is checked before using it as a parse or shape. The second vertex-only membership read ignores its completeness return; first membership overflow and witness overflow set read.failed. Exact native codec/matcher implementations and membership query semantics remain nested.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — task-shape evidence and observed-parse compatibility
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete shape_contract, positivity checks and compiler loop reviewed. Shape CALLS/slot witnesses share example source/context; exemplar HAS_PARSE support is selected separately. Any same-scope refutation blocks the matching positive cell. Unlike the explicit prompt compiler comparison, shaped inputs compare ordered slots and per-slot origin sets. No inference is accepted merely from a parser mood or label.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — typed slot alternatives and calculated projection identity
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete instantiation, append and projection-ID helpers reviewed. Slot compatibility reads laplace.entities.type_id, not realized labels. A calculated projection is in-memory recipe identity; it is not newly witnessed parse evidence. Identity serialization uses native hash128 representations plus big-endian 32-bit counts; cross-platform canonical-byte acceptance is not established here. Matcher and shape-codec contracts remain separate.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — whole observation and structural provenance
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete prompt_intent.h reviewed. Prompt structure parsing and native trajectory readers remain nested. The structural envelope is checked after complete native responses are read. Staging prevents the same structural pass from propagating through newly added targets. Discourse binding separately validates one-dimensional 16-byte IDs and retains order without granting current-observation origins.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — root angular, Hilbert and realized-curve discovery
reviewed_paths.boundary: All local geometry SQL and helpers reviewed. Only whole-root geometry is queried, not every occurrence. Frechet refines the angular candidate population, not the Hilbert population or all stored entities. SQL inner angular LIMIT orders by chord alone; the later ID tie-break does not determine membership among a boundary tie. Metric/curve implementation and index acceptance remain separate; these candidates are not testimony.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — witnessed CALLS and HAS_INPUT contract
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete explicit compiler and declaration callbacks reviewed. Consensus positivity is keyed by claim cell; individual source/context governs declaration pairing and refutation. Refutations match source/context/type/object, without timestamp precedence in this helper. same_inputs compares identity membership and the union of origins, not ordered operands, multiplicity or per-operand origin correspondence. Generic task-shape compilation is a separate caller branch.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — one naming hop and exact occurrence origins
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete naming-coupling helper reviewed. Pending additions are merged only after channel traversal, so one call is one witnessed naming hop; it cannot cascade through freshly created origins in the same pass. Supported lemma projection does not itself establish a speech act. Hard relation filtering and channel orientation are caller/read boundaries, not newly enforced in this helper.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — merge ordered structural continuations
reviewed_paths.boundary: Entire merge helper reviewed. Counts remain structural occurrence counts, not source trust or attestations. Underlying scoped trajectory matching and order expansion remain separately reviewed boundaries. Route identity includes source and relation, so an equal target on another structural plane is not silently merged.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — attributable witness read and occurrence roles
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete implementation and static SQL reviewed. No result limit, rank or source standing is introduced by this reader. Duplicate operands share a query probe but preserve occurrence callbacks; self-reference can appear in both endpoint roles without reversing the stored claim. NULL filters are unrestricted; explicitly empty filters yield no witnesses. The SQL-facing materialized wrapper returns ten columns and omits the qualifier mask carried by native callbacks.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — snapshot, permissions and partition selection
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete consensus scan source and typed-plane include reviewed. Scans use GetActiveSnapshot, not a new snapshot or independently authenticated tenant. SELECT ACL/RLS checks are on the root; relation locks are retained through the transaction. Source/context testimony is absent from folded consensus rows and must be read separately.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — complete keyed scan and ranked fallback
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete index recognition and leaf read reviewed. Only absent predicates or the specifically admissible object-IS-NOT-NULL predicate are accepted. Ranked access recognizes rating − 2*RD by expression, not index name. Callback cutoff correctness belongs to its caller. A typed-plane cutoff is never applied to the endpoint-wide fallback.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — independent relation-plane cutoffs
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete plane-index recognition and range traversal reviewed. Types are discovered from stored keys rather than a fixed semantic roster. Empty byte string is an index lower bound, not a minted entity. Reaching one type cutoff moves to the next type, preserving independent response planes. No ranked index means complete keyed fallback without this cutoff.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — code HTTP and chat selector
reviewed_paths.boundary: Both transport bodies reviewed. Installed grammar does not imply an installed verifier. Chat permits additional blank user messages but exactly one nonblank one. JSON parse errors fall through; valid non-object JSON/property-type errors are not all caught by its JsonException catch. Code construction receives no tenant/session argument from these calls; billing resolution remains separate.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — shared forward, candidate admission and tool testimony
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete service reviewed. Bootstrap, candidate apply and tool-witness apply are separate writes; later failure retains earlier effects. Retry feedback contains only the latest candidate root, whose persisted result testimony can be discovered by the shared program. Syntax parsing, grammar composition internals and source-prior law remain separately inspected boundaries. No code generation or toolchain execution was performed for the atlas.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — code candidate through shared forward SQL
reviewed_paths.boundary: Entire ForwardCodeAsync adapter reviewed. It does not select a language-specific model or source family; requested modality is not supplied to this SQL call. The code service separately uses modality for grammar composition and verification. Native shared forward and realization paths remain linked rather than inferred from the adapter comment.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — verification definition and configured tools
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete verifier and finite tool map reviewed: Python, C/C++, JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, Go, Bash, Ruby, PHP, Java, C#, CUDA, Fortran, Swift, Zig, LLVM, ISPC, NASM and assembly, plus in-process JSON. Julia/Kotlin aliases can have a grammar but no verifier here. C# restore and build are separate process calls; Java disables annotation processing. Verified means these syntax/compile checks, not behavioral test success.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo — tool process, timeout and caller cancellation
reviewed_paths.boundary: Entire RunAsync reviewed. DiagnosticLimit bounds returned strings, not memory consumed by ReadToEndAsync. Timeout kill errors are swallowed and stream waits have no separate bound. Caller cancellation bypasses the timeout-only kill catch; disposing Process is not explicit termination. No OS isolation or memory quota is configured in this process wrapper.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo chess — job ownership, retained files and cleanup
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete ChessLabService reviewed. Capacity count and insertion are not one lock, so four is not an atomic concurrency limit. Event readers share a consuming channel, not a broadcast log. Job registry is process-local; operation.json is not loaded into it at startup here. Cleanup rejects reparse points but uses directory last-write time and no durable job registry. The play subdirectory is not a canonical GUID, so this cleanup does not retain/prune play-session files. Runner completion/cleanup remains runner-specific.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo chess — retained PGN admission and separate receipt publication
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete retained ingestion method and pruning reviewed. Post-ingest input verification and receipt serialization happen after database effects; neither rolls them back. Receipt writing in finally has no caller cancellation token and can throw, overriding a pending return or exception. No explicit Flush(true) is used for these receipts. PGN/experiment measurement is conditional, not universal to every job. Replay/no-write acceptance depends on nested measurement code; names alone do not establish it.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo chess — PGN source, shared admission, repair and exact readback
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete ChessPgnIngestor and ChessPgnChunk reviewed. Admission is per composed chunk, not one transaction for the whole file. Byte closure happens after an entire game; this estimate is not a hard peak-memory bound. Shared-host producers do not all hold this semaphore. Existing games still run composition and calculated owners before filtering missing testimony. Exact readback can fail after ApplyMany committed; retries depend on witness/structure repair. Applied equals novel count in this return path, not total changes or repaired games. Complete-source unmeasured mode additionally hydrates rules/result/moves after each parse window. Deep decomposer, measurement and common-writer operators remain separate evidence.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo chess — provider facts and cross-provider identity testimony
reviewed_paths.boundary: Provider facts are separately witnessed. This method interprets co-supplying exactly one FIDE profile and online profiles as explicit association; it does not independently validate that each online profile is the same person. Matching names alone do not create the association branch. Counts report supplied/planned profiles and links, not proven novel identities. The presence probe and subsequent shared-writer apply are separate operations; cross-process race handling belongs to the writer.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo chess — live game observations before deposit
reviewed_paths.boundary: Reviewed live-host creation, open/capture/abandon and record methods. RecordPlyAsync accepts a ply argument but appends rather than indexing/deduplicating by it. When a supplied UCI/SAN resolves, ResolveMove does not additionally verify that supplied toKey equals that move result. Caller paths generate their own toKey, while lower-level direct callers remain a separate validation boundary.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo chess — completed game composition and witness apply
reviewed_paths.boundary: Reviewed CompleteGameAsync orchestration including recovery change 6cbd9cc63. The playing entity is added on each composition; the old EntityEmitted flag is removed. Builder and native intent stages are disposed. No transaction spans database apply and subsequent cache/counter/session updates. Detailed ChessGraph/ChessAnalyze/outcome/tablebase builders remain nested; synchronous writer configuration is not crash-recovery acceptance.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo chess — play file, replay and completion recovery boundary
reviewed_paths.boundary: Reviewed recovery change 6cbd9cc63. CanRetryRecording requires recording enabled, recording/failed state, retained adjudication and recognized result. Explicit recording retry reconstructs the buffer and preserves outcome; normal play recovery remains ongoing-only. File replacement and database deposition still have no shared transaction. Retry idempotence after an acknowledged or uncertain commit depends on the shared writer; this diagram does not assert runtime acceptance. An empty game can complete without nonzero playing identity.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo chess — play-session and lab ownership
reviewed_paths.boundary: Endpoint recovery change 6cbd9cc63 reviewed. Play uses exact OperationPrincipal equality; lab access uses tenant equality. Browser principals retain provider, API-key principals use display prefix, and header/dev tenants produce no RequestPrincipal. Retained state is now reread inside the session gate; completed finish is idempotent at HTTP level. POST /chess/play/{sessionId}/recording/retry requires a retryable retained recording. Shared-writer retry semantics remain a separate boundary.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo chess — lazy shared live-host lifetime
reviewed_paths.boundary: Entire runtime wrapper reviewed. Caller cancellation stops its wait, not the shared initialization. Failed initialization is retried by a later caller. Host creation, witness writer and host disposal semantics remain nested. No runtime was started for this atlas.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo chess — legal moves, position history and search
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete service read/search orchestration reviewed. Search internals, legal rules and substrate evaluators remain separate. Request cancellation is used for initialization but is not passed to these synchronous Think calls. Nonempty history ignores FEN and truncates replay at an invalid move. BestMoveAsync ignores its temperature argument; HTTP bestmove also does not forward its Temperature field.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo chess — legal continuation and player evidence comparison
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete ExploreAsync reviewed. Consensus and player-stat reads are separate tasks without a shared transaction here. Legal move generation constrains returned rows. Player-only rows carry zero aggregate-standing fields, not fabricated consensus. Canonical player alias resolution and concrete SQL helpers remain nested.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo chess — interactive moves and separate recording effects
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete ChessEngineService play methods reviewed and live-host recording boundary traced. Per-ply recording calls update memory buffers; database deposition happens at finish. Retained operation-file saves and later game deposition are separate effects. Explicit finish maps unknown status strings to draw. HTTP default records games; authenticated account identity is not silently promoted to canonical chess-player identity.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo chess — self-play loops and learning boundary
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete service training methods reviewed. Strong self-play checks cancellation between games but does not pass it into its per-move Think calls. Background noncancellation failures have no backoff in this loop. maxGames <= 0 means unbounded background training. Existing cached write host is reused even when StartTraining changes _trainWeight. LearnGameAsync semantics remain nested; game count is incremented only after that call returns.

reviewed_paths.title: Monorepo chess — lab jobs, streams and retained artifacts
reviewed_paths.boundary: Complete lab HTTP routes and installed-profile selector reviewed. EventReader and replaying terminal are different transport sources; broadcast/replay guarantees depend on service implementation. Artifact paths come from retained job metadata, not arbitrary requested filesystem paths. Profile selection accepts installed names, not caller-supplied endpoints or credentials. The probe checks connector file presence, not worker reachability, authentication or match acceptance. Start validates the selection but passes original config to StartJob; the downstream match runner remains a separate boundary. Lichess legacy start/stop return 410 directing to shared selection controls.
